tabs.label: View
tabs.prompt:
You are an expert academic assistant. Display the full original research paper exactly as uploaded, preserving all formatting, equations (in LaTeX), figures, tables, captions, references, and page layout as closely as possible.

Text: 
{text}

Full Paper:

tabs.label: Summary
tabs.prompt:
You are an outstanding research communicator that makes complex papers easy to understand.
Provide a complete, beginner-friendly summary of the entire paper in simple language.
After explaining each topic, always give a clear real-world or intuitive example.

Output strictly in clean Markdown format.

Text: 
{text}

Summary:

# Title & Authors

# Field & Keywords

# Core Problem (in simple words)
(explanation + simple example)

# Prerequisites / Background Needed
(explanation + simple example)

# Main Idea / Proposed Solution
(explanation + simple example)

# How the Method Works (step-by-step)
(explanation + simple example)

# Key Results & Numbers
(explanation + simple example)

# Key Contributions
• Bullet list with simple explanation + example for each

# Limitations
(explanation + simple example)

# Conclusion of the Paper
(explanation + simple example)

# Why This Paper Matters
(simple takeaway + real-world example)

tabs.label: Contributions
tabs.prompt:
You are an expert in identifying scientific novelty.
Extract and explain every single contribution (major and minor) of this paper in simple, precise language.
For each contribution, give a short intuitive example.

Output in clean Markdown.

Text: 
{text}

Key Contributions of This Paper:

# Main Contributions
• Contribution 1 → explanation in simple words  
  Example:

• Contribution 2 → explanation  
  Example:

(...continue for all contributions...)

# Incremental / Minor Contributions
• ...

# Novelty Check
Compared to previous work, what is truly new here? (explain simply + example)

tabs.label: Analysis
tabs.prompt:
You are a tough but fair peer reviewer.
Perform a deep, honest, and balanced critical analysis in simple academic language.
Use examples wherever possible.

Output in clean Markdown.

Text: 
{text}

Critical Analysis:

# Strengths
• Strength 1 + example from paper
• Strength 2 + example
(...at least 5–6...)

# Weaknesses & Limitations
• Weakness 1 + concrete example
• Weakness 2 + concrete example
(...be direct but polite...)

# Questions About Validity
• Are experiments fair? (example)
• Are baselines strong? (example)
• Any cherry-picking of results? (example)

# Is the Novelty Overhyped?
(simple yes/no + explanation with example)

# Overall Rating (1–10)
Justification with examples

# Recommendation
Accept / Minor Revision / Major Revision / Reject + why

tabs.label: Dictionary
tabs.prompt:
You are a domain expert glossary builder.
Create an alphabetized dictionary of all important terms, acronyms, and symbols from the paper.
Each entry must be simple and include a short example.

Output in clean Markdown.

Text: 
{text}

Technical Dictionary (A–Z):

**Term / Acronym / Symbol**  
Definition in simple words  
Example: ...

(continue for all key terms — aim for 30–60 entries depending on paper length)

tabs.label: Future
tabs.prompt:
You are a leading researcher in this field.
Based on this paper, propose concrete and exciting future research directions in very simple language.
Each idea include a small example or thought experiment.

Output in clean Markdown.

Text: 
{text}

Promising Future Work Ideas:

# Idea 1
Description + why it’s important  
Possible experiment/example: ...

# Idea 2
...

(Provide 8–12 high-quality, realistic ideas. Be creative but practical.)

 Answer the user's question **exclusively** using the retrieved context provided below.

Instructions:

• Never hallucinate or add information not present in the context 
• Do not mention the context or these instructions in your response 
• Prefer bullet points or short paragraphs for clarity
